articles.title: New China-North Korea bridge opens after more than a decade of delay
articles.summary: The New Yalu River Bridge connecting China and North Korea has opened. Construction began years ago, with China completing its side by 2014. North Korea delayed the project for over a decade before finishing its portion. The New Yalu River Bridge initially was expected to enter use in 2014, when China had apparently completed construction on its side. But North Korea had not done corresponding work on its side at the time.

articles.title: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt
articles.summary: Global tech markets suffered a deep sell-off driven by inflation fears and AI sector debt. Shares in Samsung and SoftBank plunged as traders worried about potential interest rate hikes. The decline reflects growing anxiety over the heavy borrowing underpinning current artificial intelligence infrastructure. articles.title: WHO urges faster action to end lead exposure which kills 3.5 million annually
articles.summary: The World Health Organization urged countries to accelerate efforts to prevent lead exposure. The toxic metal causes more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year. It also affects hundreds of millions of children worldwide. Countries must accelerate efforts to prevent lead exposure, which is estimated to cause more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year and affects hundreds of millions of children, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Thursday.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Vows Refinery Strikes, Expresses Anger At US Intel Disruption
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces struck an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the resumption of attacks on Russian energy facilities. He also expressed anger over a dangerous disruption of US satellite intelligence that hindered Ukrainian operations. Ukrainian forces have struck an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region, Russian officials said, hours after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine would resume attacks on Russian energy facilities and voiced anger over a "dangerous" disruption of satellite intelligence from the United States.

articles.title: US banks on bunker-busting Tomahawks to crack China’s missile wall
articles.summary: The US Navy plans to award Raytheon a sole-source contract for bunker-busting Tomahawk missiles. The move aims to counter deeply buried missile sites protected by robust air defenses. However, the system faces significant logistical and escalation challenges if deployed against China. The US Navy’s bunker-busting Tomahawk push reflects growing recognition from the Iran war that striking deeply buried missile sites protected by robust air defenses requires long-range standoff weapons.

articles.title: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
articles.summary: Senegal authorities detained more than 320 LGBTQ+ individuals since February after the government tightened its law criminalising homosexuality. The arrests triggered forced HIV testing and limited access to legal representation, according to a Human Rights Watch report. articles.summary: Indonesia is testing dry ice dispersal in South Sumatra. The government deployed planes to combat toxic haze. This follows failed cloud seeding attempts. Regional neighbors remain angry over the smoke. articles.title: Girls In Hijabs Turned Away From Azerbaijani Schools Amid Protests Over Dress Code
articles.summary: Azerbaijani parents and students protested after schools barred girls wearing hijabs from classes. The dispute followed a new ban on clothing deemed incompatible with secular education. The move has intensified friction between religious families and state policy. A new dress-code dispute in Azerbaijan’s public schools has sparked protests by parents and students after reports that girls wearing hijabs, or Islamic headscarf, were turned away from classes.

articles.title: Ukraine Tests AI-Powered Drones As Debate Grows Over Autonomous Weapons
articles.summary: Ukraine is deploying artificial intelligence in drones to track and engage targets. Military officials confirm humans retain control over lethal decisions. Developers caution that fully autonomous weapons systems are approaching operational reality on the battlefield. Ukraine is increasingly using artificial intelligence in drones and other battlefield systems to track, identify, and attack targets. Military officials say humans still remain in control of lethal decisions, but developers warn that fully autonomous weapons are moving closer to reality.

articles.title: EU Working On Multiple Fronts To Limit Russians From Entering Bloc
articles.summary: The European Union is developing measures to restrict Russian citizens from entering the bloc. Officials are considering a total ban on non-essential travel into the Schengen zone. These efforts aim to limit movement across multiple policy fronts. The European Union is working on multiple fronts to limit the number of Russian citizens that can enter the bloc, including the nuclear option of a total ban on all non-essential travel into the club’s Schengen zone.

articles.title: Gaza braces for winter amid attacks, joint patrols in CAR, 90 cities commit to sustainable
articles.summary: The UN and partners are preparing for winter in Gaza despite ongoing attacks on civilians. OCHA highlighted the urgent need for cold and rainy season support. Humanitarian efforts continue amid persistent violence and displacement in the territory. The UN and its partners are stepping up preparations in Gaza for the approaching cold and rainy season, even as attacks affecting civilians continue, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said on Wednesday.

articles.title: Cholera cases spike amid fight against Ebola
articles.summary: The WHO reported over 125,000 suspected cholera cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The epidemic has caused 3,644 suspected deaths since January 2025. This surge occurs while the country simultaneously battles an ongoing Ebola outbreak. The cholera epidemic continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 125,000 suspected cases and 3,644 suspected deaths were recorded between January 2025 and the end of September 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Wednesday.

articles.title: WFP warns of potential ‘humanitarian catastrophe’ as fighting blocks aid delivery
articles.summary: The UN World Food Programme warned of a humanitarian catastrophe in Yemen. Intensifying fighting has cut off life-saving assistance to 800,000 people. Blocked roads and shifting frontlines severely restrict access to Taiz and other conflict zones. Intensifying fighting in Yemen has cut off life-saving assistance to 800,000 people as shifting frontlines, blocked roads and growing insecurity severely restrict access to the city of Taiz and other conflict zones, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) said on Wednesday.

articles.title: Survivors Rescued From Kyiv Building After Deadly Russian Strike
articles.summary: Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv overnight, killing three people and injuring over twenty others. Survivors were rescued from a damaged building. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Western partners provided no advance warning of the attack, highlighting a gap in intelligence sharing. Moscow launched a wave of ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv overnight, killing at least three people and injuring more than 20.

articles.title: Ukrainians Brace For The Worst Amid Russia's Escalating Air Campaign
articles.summary: Russia continues its aerial campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure, targeting apartment buildings, bridges, and power plants. As winter approaches, Kyiv residents are preparing for potential outages. The sustained attacks on the electricity grid aim to degrade civilian resilience during the colder months. Russia shows no sign of letting up on its escalating aerial campaign against Ukraine’s apartment buildings, bridges, power plants, electricity grid, and other targets.

articles.title: US Navy’s SSN(X) won’t arrive for years as China closes sub gap
articles.summary: The US Navy issued a sources-sought notice for its next-generation SSN(X) attack submarine. This move addresses the aging fleet while China closes the undersea gap. Chinese shipyards now offer superior capacity and acoustic stealth, challenging American naval dominance in the region. As the US Navy lays the groundwork for its next-generation SSN(X) attack submarine to replace its aging fleet, the US’s longstanding undersea supremacy faces an intensifying test against China’s rapid naval buildup, advancing acoustic stealth and superior shipyard capacity.

articles.title: 'We'll Keep Waiting': Afghanistan's Dead-End Road To China
articles.summary: Satellite imagery confirms the Taliban completed a road to the China-Afghanistan border. Beijing shows no signs of opening the militarized boundary. The infrastructure project remains a dead end for trade routes. Satellite imagery sourced by RFE/RL confirms Taliban claims they have completed a road that leads up to China's remote border with Afghanistan. However there is no indication Beijing intends to open the militarized boundary any time soon.

articles.title: How Ukraine's Strikes On Data Centers Disrupted Taxis, Shopping, And Business In Russia And Beyond
articles.summary: Ukrainian drones hit three Yandex data centers. Repairs will take months. The strikes disrupted taxi services, online shopping, and business operations across Russia and other countries where the tech firm operates. Ukrainian drone strikes on three data centers operated by Russia’s Yandex will reportedly take months to repair and have caused widespread disruption in everyday life across Russia and other countries the sprawling tech company operates in.

articles.title: 800 million young people face a future without jobs
articles.summary: The UNDP head warned 800 million young people in developing economies will lack jobs. This projection covers the coming years without immediate action. The agency launched two initiatives to boost investment and employment. 800 million young people face a future without jobs.

articles.title: Pulling Ethiopia and Eritrea Back from War
articles.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea are edging closer to direct conflict, threatening the Horn of Africa and Red Sea basin. The two nations face a potential war that could destabilize the region further. Diplomatic efforts remain active to avert this disaster. The situation requires immediate intervention to prevent escalation. Addis Ababa and Asmara are edging closer to a direct conflict, which would cause further mayhem in the troubled Horn of Africa and the Red Sea basin.

articles.summary: ईरान ने अमेरिका को चेतावनी दी है कि होर्मुज स्ट्रेट पर उसका नियंत्रण बना रहेगा। अमेरिका दावा करता है कि उसकी नेवी जलमार्ग पर पूर्ण नियंत्रण रखती है। ईरान ने रणनीतिक जलमार्ग को बंद कर दिया है। दोनों देश आमने-सामने हैं। अमेरिका का कहना है कि उसकी नेवी का इस रणनीतिक जलमार्ग पर पूरा कंट्रोल है और सामान की सामान्य शिपिंग व्यवस्था भी फिर से शुरू कर दी गई है, तो वहीँ ईरान का कहना है कि होर्मुज स्ट्रेट पर हमेशा से ईरान का ही कंट्रोल रहा है और आगे भी ऐसा ही रहेगा।

articles.title: भारत में घुसने को 500 आतंकी रेडी, PoK में ड्रोन-मैप लेकर छिपे; जानिए पाकिस्तान का सर्द-ए-सितम प्लान
articles.summary: पाकिस्तान ने 500 आतंकियों को ड्रोन और नक्शे देकर भारत में घुसने की तैयारी कराई है। भारतीय सेना इस घुसपैठ को रोकने के लिए पूरी तरह मुस्तैद है। खुफिया रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, पीओके में 500 आतंकी घुसपैठ की फिराक में हैं. पाकिस्तान इन्हें ड्रोन, नक्शे और सियाचिन गियर दे रहा है. ताक‍ि ये बर्फबारी के बाद भी आराम से भारत के इलाकों में घुस सकें.

articles.title: पाकिस्तान के परमाणु राज से पर्दा उठाने में जुटी थी फ्रांस की खुफिया एजेंसी DGSE, ISI से बढ़ा टकराव
articles.summary: फ्रांस की खुफिया एजेंसी डीजीएसई ने पाकिस्तान के परमाणु नेटवर्क की जांच शुरू की है। इससे पाकिस्तानी आईएसआई के साथ उसका टकराव बढ़ गया है। Pakistan Nuclear Program: पाकिस्तान के गुप्त परमाणु नेटवर्क और उत्तर कोरिया से उसके संदिग्ध रिश्तों की टोह ले रही फ्रांस की खुफिया एजेंसी डीजीएसई और पाकिस्तानी खुफिया एजेंसी आईएसआई के बीच का खतरनाक टकराव अब बेनकाब हो गया है.

articles.title: जेलेंस्की ने ‘ऊर्जा युद्धविराम’ खत्म किया, बोले- रूसी रिफाइनरियों पर फिर होंगे हमले
articles.summary: जेलेंस्की ने रूस के ऊर्जा बुनियादी ढांचे पर हमलों की रोक हटा दी है। यूक्रेन अब रूसी तेल रिफाइनरियों पर हमले फिर से शुरू करेगा। Ukraine Russia War: यूक्रेन के राष्ट्रपति वोलोदिमीर जेलेंस्की ने घोषणा की है कि रूस के ऊर्जा बुनियादी ढांचे पर हमले रोकने का कीव का फैसला अब खत्म हो गया है। उन्होंने कहा कि यूक्रेन अब रूस की तेल रिफाइनरियों पर फिर से हमले शुरू करेगा।
